subject: Used versus Total data in lavaan

messages.author: b5f242e7eb90c7c9
messages.subject: Used versus Total data in lavaan
parts:
I have a dataset with missing data, and I have set up a model to account for missing data using direct dependent variable method. However, I get the following information from lavaan output:

                                                                     Used       Total
  Number of observations                           230         529

Does it mean that 230 participants have complete data, or that only 230 participants were included in the entire analysis (and thus the treatment of missing data analysis was not successful)? Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Used versus Total data in lavaan
parts:
It means 230 subjestcts were inclded in the analysis. How did you intend to handle missing data?
If youn expected to use Full Information Maximum Liklihood (FIML), including all subjects that have data in at least 1 variable you need to include the argument missing="fiml" when you use cfa/sem. If you used this argument and still have this, would happend because the ecluded subejects have missing data in all the variables included in the analysis

When you ask a question like this, please share the mode, and lavaan call, so we can have a better idea of what you are doing and where the error might be

parts:
Thanks. Let's assume that I want to estimate the covariance matrix with missing data, with items a,b,c, and d, with m being an auxiliary variable. Can I use the following syntax, having four latent variables of a, b, c, and d to directly predict m (i.e., direct dependent variable method)? Do the following syntax makes sense?

Model.missing <- '

# specifying four latent variables for each item
afs ~ 1*a
bfs ~ 1*b
cfs ~ 1*c
dfs ~ 1*d

# specifying no item intercept, so that item mean = latent variables means (e.g., afs = 1*a)
# residual for latent variables are also omitted, so that the estimation of a (in afs) involve measurement error
a ~ 0*1
b ~ 0*1
c ~ 0*1
d ~ 0*1

afs ~~ 0*afs
bfs ~~ 0*bfs
cfs ~~ 0*cfs
dfs ~~ 0*dfs

afs ~~ bfs + cfs + dfs
bfs ~~ cfs + dfs
cfs ~~ dfs

m ~ afs + bfs + cfs +dfs
'

Modeling.missing = cfa(
  Model.missing, data = Dataset, estimator = "MLR", missing="fiml"
)

# the following command output estimated covariance matrix for the item's latent variable
cov.lv(Modeling.fullsample)

messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: Re: Used versus Total data in lavaan
parts:
Chester

You dont have latent variables here, and are adding a bunch of constraints that I dont think make sense. If the idea its to use a single indicator variable to define latent variables, i this case you will reach the same withput the single indicator variable, just suing th variables directly

Model.missing <- '
a ~~ b + c + d
b ~~  c + d
c ~~ d

m ~ a + b + c + d
'

Modeling.missing = cfa(Model.missing, data = Dataset, estimator = "MLR", missing="fiml")
summary(Modeling.missing, standardized=T)

In the Est column you will have the covariance estimates, and in the std.all column you will have the correlation estimates

If you want to use single indicator factors need to defined them like this for example
'
ph_a =~ 1*a
ph_a ~~ NA*ph_a
ph_a ~0*1
a ~~ 0*a
'
In this form, I am moin the item variance to the latent factor variance, and the mean estimated at the item level. You can estimated in different ways, like the next one.
'
ph_a =~ NA*a
ph_a ~~ 1*ph_a
ph_a ~0*1
a ~~ 0*a
'
This one standardized the latent variable and the factor loadings will be the indicator standard deviation. Depends how you want to interpret this phantom latent variable.

But for the simple example, you presented, I dont think his would be neccesary
